Using the supplied character sheet as the sole character reference, create one head-and-shoulders character reference sheet containing exactly four panels in a strict two-by-two grid.

The overall canvas is square. All four panels must be identical squares with exactly the same width and height. Use two equal-width columns and two equal-height rows, with perfectly aligned boundaries and narrow, uniform light gray gutters. Keep panel sizes fixed and adjust the character’s framing within each panel. No merged cells, unequal panels, inset images, or irregular collage layouts.

Every panel shows exactly one head-and-shoulders portrait of the same character. Strictly preserve the reference character’s facial identity, apparent age, skin tone, eyes, hairstyle, hair color, clothing, and accessories. Retain the reference image’s visual style and material rendering. Use a plain light gray studio background, soft even diffused lighting, and a level eye-height camera throughout. Keep a calm neutral expression in all four views.

Arrange the views in this exact order:

Top left: Frontal head-and-shoulders portrait. The head and shoulders face directly toward the camera, with the eyes looking straight ahead.

Top right: Left three-quarter head-and-shoulders portrait. Turn the head and shoulders together approximately forty-five degrees toward screen right. The nose points toward screen right, primarily exposing the character’s left side of the face, with both eyes visible.

Bottom left: Right three-quarter head-and-shoulders portrait. Turn the head and shoulders together approximately forty-five degrees toward screen left. The nose points toward screen left, primarily exposing the character’s right side of the face, with both eyes visible.

Bottom right: Exact ninety-degree profile head-and-shoulders portrait facing screen left. Show only one eye and a clear side silhouette of the forehead, nose, lips, and chin. The shoulders follow the same side-facing orientation.

Maintain identical portrait scale, headroom, and eye height across all four panels. Show the complete hairstyle, head, neck, and shoulders without clipping the top of the head. Keep each portrait centered within its own panel.

Preserve the correct physical placement of asymmetric facial features, hair details, and accessories as the character turns. Do not create opposite views by simply mirroring the image. Keep the same character identity across all four views.

Output exactly four equally sized square panels in one regular two-by-two grid. No full-body views, extra people, repeated viewpoints, text, numbers, labels, logos, or watermarks.
